//! A single queue: its attributes, messages and bookkeeping.
//!
//! The queue knows nothing about other queues or the clock's owner; the
//! broker passes `now` in and coordinates dead-letter moves.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, HashSet};

use crate::attributes::Attributes;

pub const MAX_MESSAGES: usize = 100_000;
const DEDUP_WINDOW: u64 = 300;
const MIN_DEDUP_PRUNE_LEN: usize = 1024;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Message {
    pub id: u64,
    pub body: String,
    pub sent_at: u64,
    pub receive_count: u64,
    pub first_received_at: Option<u64>,
    pub group_id: Option<String>,
    pub sequence_number: Option<u64>,
    /// The message is delayed while `now < delayed_until`.
    pub delayed_until: u64,
    /// The message is in flight while `now < invisible_until`.
    pub invisible_until: u64,
    /// The latest receipt handle issued for this message.
    pub handle: Option<u64>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum State {
    Delayed,
    InFlight,
    Visible,
}

impl Message {
    pub fn state(&self, now: u64) -> State {
        if now < self.delayed_until {
            State::Delayed
        } else if now < self.invisible_until {
            State::InFlight
        } else {
            State::Visible
        }
    }
}

/// What `ReceiveMessage` does with one examined message.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Step {
    Deliver(u64),
    DeadLetter(u64),
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Counts {
    pub visible: u64,
    pub in_flight: u64,
    pub delayed: u64,
}

/// The original message of a deduplication id.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub struct Accepted {
    pub accepted_at: u64,
    pub message_id: u64,
    pub sequence_number: u64,
}

pub struct Queue {
    pub attributes: Attributes,
    /// Messages in arrival order, keyed by an ever-growing arrival index.
    messages: BTreeMap<u64, Message>,
    next_arrival: u64,

content.text:
I made four small refactoring commits on `main`. `cargo test` passes in full and clippy is clean.

The crate was already in reasonable shape. I made targeted changes and didn't restructure it.

1. **`90569e6`, named attribute ranges.** The `VisibilityTimeout` and `DelaySeconds` limits were bare numbers repeated in the attribute parser and the message commands. Each now has one constant.
2. **`0c1af6e`, required-parameter getters.** Handlers called `require()` and then `.expect("required")` on the typed getter. `required_string` and `required_integer` fold the presence check into the read, so the invariant is now an error path instead of a panic. `require()` still runs first in each handler, which keeps the SPEC section 2 check order. A shared `missing_parameter` constructor replaces a duplicated helper.
3. **`5c4d97f`, `Command` enum.** Dispatch matched on strings. The command is now parsed into an enum in `Request::parse`, so the match is exhaustive and every `InvalidRequest` cause lives in one place.
4. **`d926acd`, small tidy.**
   - `plan_receive` takes the `u64` `MaxMessages` directly instead of casting to `usize`.
   - The `is_expired` closure in `Queue::expire` was built before the early return that makes it unnecessary, so I inlined it.
   - This commit has two small changes in it, so it isn't strictly one kind of change.

My first commit was broken: a script failed partway and I committed before noticing. I amended it once the tests passed, so the history has no broken commit.

**What I left alone:**
- `Message` and `Queue` still have public fields. Narrowing them would touch every call site.
- `set_queue_attributes` still looks the queue up twice.
- `create_queue` still computes the dead-letter configuration twice.

I can do any of these next if you want.
